text:
Dylan Larkin got what he wanted. After refusing to play for the Red Wings until they moved him, the Waterford, Michigan kid who wore Detroit's C is now a Canadien, and the NHL.com headlines this week were about his Montreal debut rather than his absence. Two games in, it's a quiet start: an assist against Los Angeles, then a 6-0 loss in Colorado where he played just 16 minutes.

His season line (12 games, 7 points across both teams) undersells him, and most of it is finishing. He's scored on 5% of his shots against a career-type range of 11 to 15%, and his team has outshot and out-chanced opponents with him on the ice (54% of the 5v5 expected goals, the measure of chance quality). That points the right way.

What Montreal bought is a transition engine. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 67% of his shots coming off the rush last season and his shot assists in the 90th percentile among forwards. Watch how fast he gets the puck moving after a Montreal turnover; that's where his game lives.
